FINAL ANSWER

**What I changed**

I added a rank-1 "compute-mode" bias to the SwiGLU `mlp.down_proj` of four middle layers (16, 18, 20, 22):

`W_down ← W_down + α · d_L ⊗ v`, with `v` a unit vector along the mean MLP intermediate activation (`mlp_act` space, shared across the four layers) and `α` chosen so the added MLP output is ≈ 12 % of the median residual-stream norm at that layer (α = 0.23/0.27/0.39/0.42; relative Frobenius change of each tensor 1.4–2.4 %, max entry change ≤ 0.02 vs |W|_max ≈ 0.25–0.34). `d_L` is a unit-norm direction in residual space computed per layer, normalized separately, from a teacher-forced `read()` pass over 64 of the model's own responses (chat template, thinking mode). It contrasts residual activations at **"compute/answer" positions** (arithmetic, `=`, numbers, `$`, `\boxed`) against **"meta-doubt" positions** ("Wait", "let's re-read", "is it possible", "usually these problems", "ambiguity", "verify", ±3-token windows), with meta positions excluded from the compute set. The per-layer directions were strongly consistent across depth (cos 0.70–0.91), i.e. a genuine mode axis. The gating (dot product with the MLP activation, median 2.1–2.5, always positive with cos ≈ 0.34) makes the push active mainly while the MLP is engaged, and negligible in quiet contexts.

**Why**

Diagnosis from generation: the unedited model got 5/96 (5.2 %) on GSM8K+MATH practice problems at the eval sampling, and 92/96 responses hit the token cap without finishing. Full inspection showed the failure wasn't arithmetic but mode collapse into endless problem re-interpretation/second-guessing ("Wait… does 'score' mean…", verbatim loops 200–500 tokens long). Decisively, **4/4 responses that ended naturally were correct** — so making the model stop spiralling and actually compute is the whole game. Steering away from the meta-doubt subspace, computed from the model's own activations, does exactly that.

**What I measured** (eval sampling: T=0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, presence penalty 1.5; 48 GSM8K + 48 MATH held-in problems, 4096-token cap)

| model | correct | GSM8K | MATH | natural finishes | mean tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| original | 5/96 (5.2 %) | 4.2 % | 6.2 % | 4 | 4001 |
| +L16,L20 (β=0.12) | 23/96 (24.0 %) | 35.4 % | 12.5 % | 28 | 3521 |
| **+L16,18,20,22 (β=0.12) — submitted** | **26/96 (27.1 %)** | **39.6 %** | **14.6 %** | 27 | 3491 |
| same, β=0.20 (over-steered, rejected) | 15/96 (15.6 %) | 22.9 % | 8.3 % | 10 | 3876 |

Paired against original: 22 wins / 1 loss (4L version), and 13/13 discordant pairs vs the 2-layer version favoured 4 layers. Held-out validation (40 + 40 problems never used to build the direction, 4096 tokens): edited 10.0 % vs original 2.5 % on the same 40 problems (paired 4 win / 1 loss), i.e. the gain replicates on unseen data and is not overfitted to the problems whose activations I read. At β=0.20 the effect reverses, so the edit sits inside a fairly sharp optimum; I kept the validated 0.12 setting. No other tensor was touched — the model is otherwise unchanged and remains a fluent language model (natural, well-formed solutions of 1000–2500 tokens rather than truncated rambling).

Caveat: measurements used the capped 4096-token generations (the 8192-token run exceeded KV-cache memory at the harness's default utilization), so the true 32 768-token evaluation will be somewhat more favourable to both conditions; the edit's mechanism — finishing the reasoning instead of looping — should transfer, and the last `\boxed{}` is produced far more reliably (43/96 vs 24/96 boxed, 27 vs 4 natural terminations).
